metadata.title: Report on Social Desirability, Midpoint and Extreme Responding in TALIS 2013 (EN)
authors: Fons J. R. Van de Vijver

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2013 teacher survey data for lower secondary teachers (ISCED Level 2) from 18 participating countries that administered the social desirability scale items. The analytic sample was restricted to teachers with valid, complete responses on the 10-item social desirability scale and permission for inclusion; additional exclusions removed teachers with highly implausible response patterns (e.g., selecting the maximum option for all items) and those with incomplete/invalid responses. The paper does not report the use of TALIS sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures, so the weighting approach for complex survey design is not documented in the provided text. For analysts using TALIS microdata, complex survey weights and appropriate variance estimation are typically required to produce population-representative estimates; however, this working paper focuses on measurement invariance, correlations, and ANCOVA-based corrections rather than PV-based achievement estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables in this report are response-style constructs (social desirability, extreme responding, midpoint responding, and a general response style factor) and TALIS teacher questionnaire scale scores, not cognitive achievement PVs. Missing-data handling is not reported in the sense of an imputation/deletion rule for item nonresponse within the analytic modeling; instead, the paper describes exclusions of countries without the scale, non-availability of some countries’ data, and removal of teachers with incomplete/invalid responses and implausible response patterns. Therefore, the missing-data strategy is only partially described and does not provide a full methodological specification for how missingness was treated beyond these exclusions.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample includes TALIS 2013 lower secondary teachers (ISCED Level 2) who (a) were in the 18 countries that administered the social desirability scale items and provided permission for inclusion, (b) had valid, complete responses on the 10-item social desirability scale, and (c) were not excluded for incomplete/omitted/invalid responses (8% of participating teachers) or for implausible response patterns (teachers who selected a score of 7 on all 10 social desirability items; less than 1% per country). Countries that did not administer the scale (14 countries) and countries that did not make their data available for analysis (Israel and Romania) were excluded from the study.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD working paper analyzes response styles in TALIS 2013 using teacher questionnaire data from 76,887 lower secondary teachers across 18 countries that administered a 10-item social desirability scale. The study first tests measurement invariance of a two-factor social desirability structure (positive and negative impression management) using multigroup confirmatory factor analysis, finding strong support for partial metric invariance but weak scalar invariance. It then integrates social desirability with extreme and midpoint responding into a general response style factor extracted via exploratory factor analysis, explaining 64% of variance, with social desirability and extreme responding loading positively and midpoint responding negatively. The paper correlates response-style factors with country-level socioeconomic and education indicators (including PISA 2012 achievement means and HDI) and with 17 core TALIS constructs at both individual and country levels. Finally, it applies ANCOVA-based correction procedures and finds negligible changes in the size and rank order of cross-cultural differences in the core constructs after controlling for response styles, suggesting limited impact on substantive country comparisons.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD Education Working Paper focused on measurement properties, correlations, and statistical correction implications for TALIS teacher questionnaire constructs rather than on machine-learning prediction. As a result, there are no ML algorithms to extract, no PV handling, and no predictive target-variable performance metrics. The main empirical outputs are invariance results, factor integration, correlation patterns, and ANCOVA-based effect-size comparisons before versus after response-style correction.
